overview.text: Hodegetria is a Mother-and-Child type in which Mary indicates Christ. The OCA relates the name and the venerated Constantinopolitan image to the Monastery of the Guides. The type is represented by numerous later icons, rather than one surviving original.

blocks.text: In the OCA’s description, the Theotokos holds Christ with her left arm and indicates him with her right hand. The meaning of the pointing gesture is given through Christ’s identification of himself as the way, truth, and life in John 14:6.

blocks.text: The entry records the Church tradition that Saint Luke painted an image of Mary from life and received her blessing. This is a traditional attribution, rather than independently established authorship for the artwork displayed here. The account follows the sacred image from Palestine to Constantinople through Empress Eudokia and Saint Pulcheria, and says it was destroyed when Constantinople fell in 1453. It names a copy at Xenophontos Monastery on Athos.
